summary: Our project aims to provide children and young people aged 7–14 with an engaging, accessible, and enjoyable introduction to the activities and responsibilities of a NASA astronaut, both on Earth and in outer space. It seeks to convey information in a concise, entertaining, and easily comprehensible manner, fostering curiosity and encouraging a deeper understanding of space exploration and the multifaceted nature of an astronaut’s work.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Orbit Cadet is a mission-based training simulator for children and young teens. The player is a cadet who must complete eight missions in order:

M-01 Neutral Buoyancy Pool – move through underwater waypoints and learn how water drag simulates weightlessness.

M-02 Launch – manage throttle to keep G-load within safe limits, stay in the ascent corridor and separate the stage on time.

M-03 Docking – approach the station and make contact slower than 1 m/s with precise alignment.

M-04 Station Operations – float through the station, collect cargo and stow it, learning that objects keep moving until something stops them.

M-05 Emergency – respond to a cabin air leak: escape the module, close the hatch to isolate it and reach the safe haven before pressure drops.

M-06 Spacewalk – work outside on a safety tether and repair three units by holding position steadily.

M-07 Moon – collect samples in one-sixth gravity and return to the lander.

M-08 Reentry – hold the correct entry angle, deploy drogue and main parachutes at the right altitudes and splash down near the recovery ship.

Each mission has a mission-control briefing, a live instrument panel (oxygen, fuel, speed, mission time), a star rating, a short quiz and a science fact. Points unlock five cadet ranks, and completing all missions unlocks a downloadable fake certificate with the player's name.
We use Phaser 3, Vite, Web Audio API, HTML5, Canvas/WebGL, JSON, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for code and desing.
